title: 0441-a-statistical-audit-of-physical-ai
universal_lens: Statistical audit of benchmark redundancy via pairwise Spearman correlations, leave-one-out ridge predictability, and Bradley–Terry ranking yields minimal unique signal across 12 physical-AI suites. Statistical audit of physical AI employs leave-one-model-out cross-validation and Gini-based utility maximization for benchmark selection.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian conformal prediction of model performance using redundant benchmark ensembles enables robust uncertainty quantification for GSI's probabilistic forecasting engine. Bayesian inference framework applies Gini coefficient and OLS residuals to quantify discrimination and marginal information in predictive models.
gse_mapping: Situationally adaptive state transitions in GSE are informed by greedy forward selection of non-redundant metrics, enabling efficient model variant discrimination. Situationally adaptive state transitions use Bradley–Terry preferences to rank benchmarks based on pairwise comparisons and residualized general capability axes.

primitives.name: Benchmark Redundancy Audit
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — the physical-AI domain doesn't transfer, but the benchmark-redundancy audit machinery (pairwise Spearman + LOO ridge predictability + greedy utility forward-selection + Bradley–Terry over benchmarks-as-judges) ports directly to pruning GSE's own metric catalog and to auditing which of GSE's model variants actually add unique signal.

primitives.assumptions: Benchmarks are independently scored; pairwise correlations capture sufficient redundancy; model performance is linearly predictable from benchmark scores.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Spearman correlations exceed 0.95, redundancy dominates interpretability.

primitives.name: Redundant Capability Inflation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The motivation: vendors report each new model on hand-picked, barely-overlapping benchmark sets, and headline averages silently double-count capabilities measured repeatedly (e.g., pointing evaluated 3–4 times within one model report).

primitives.assumptions: Inflation scales linearly with repetition count; corrected estimates are unbiased.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When R_{rep} > 3, I_{cap} exceeds C_{adj} by more than 15%.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 presents a statistical audit of physical AI benchmarks, focusing on redundancy, uniqueness, and ranking dynamics. The core insight is that pairwise Spearman correlations (ρ = 0.487) indicate moderate overlap among benchmarks, but some pairs exceed 0.8, such as EmbSpatial↔CV-Bench (ρ = 0.876). This suggests that certain benchmarks are nearly redundant, which affects how they contribute to overall utility. Forward selection identifies a minimal suite of four benchmarks—RefSpatial-Bench, MindCube, VSI-Bench, and BLINK—that capture 78.5% of total utility. This supports the idea that a small subset can approximate full benchmark coverage. Predictive uniqueness, measured via leave-one-out R², reveals that Where2Place and RefSpatial-Bench have relatively high uniqueness (low R²), while ERQA is most redundant. The ranking impact of substituting pairs shows that removing redundancy significantly alters model rankings—22 of 51 models shift by ≥3 places. These findings suggest that benchmark design must balance comprehensiveness with independence to avoid misleading model comparisons. The Bradley–Terry leaderboard further highlights the importance of domain-specific training, showing that embodiment/spatial post-trained models dominate the top ranks. Thus, the chapter establishes foundational principles for constructing robust, non-redundant benchmark suites that support both accurate evaluation and meaningful comparative analysis.
